transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you to the clinic?

I'm here because I'm feeling incredibly anxious and distressed about how my face looks, especially my nose. It feels completely crooked and asymmetrical, and I'm convinced it looks really ugly and noticeable to everyone. This worry has just been taking over my life, which is why I decided to seek help.
Do you spend a lot of time checking, comparing, or trying to hide your nose or other facial features because of how they look?

Yes, I spend hours every day checking my nose in mirrors and constantly comparing it to almost everyone I see. I also try to hide it by using heavy contouring makeup and always angling my face so people don't see it directly. When the anxiety gets too bad, I actually end up avoiding mirrors altogether just to escape looking at it.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["Body Dysmorphic Disorder", "Generalized Anxiety Disorder"], but the interview now shows a clear, persistent preoccupation with a perceived defect in appearance (nose being crooked/asymmetrical), repetitive checking/comparing, camouflaging with makeup, and mirror avoidance. This pattern strongly supports Body Dysmorphic Disorder. Generalized Anxiety Disorder is less likely because the anxiety is specifically centered on appearance rather than multiple everyday domains.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a persistent preoccupation with a perceived facial defect (nose), spends hours checking and comparing appearance, uses camouflage behaviors, and avoids mirrors due to distress. These appearance-focused obsessions and repetitive behaviors are most consistent with Body Dysmorphic Disorder rather than a broader obsessive-compulsive syndrome.
